name: CreditAccess Grameen Ltd.
reason: Indian microfinance lender whose EPS swings with the credit/regulatory cycle (INR 90.41 in 2023 to 33.24 in 2024, -63%, after earlier 2020 collapse) with 10y avg ROE 13.1%; earnings set by unforecastable rural credit cycles, failing the US bank/lender standard.

name: Godawari Power & Ispat Ltd.
reason: Captive iron-ore/pellet/steel producer with EPS set by commodity prices (INR -1.48 in 2015 to 22.28 in 2021 then 12.58 in 2025, margin 4.7%-32.9%); commodity earner with no forecastable growth route.

name: Bharat Petroleum Corp. Ltd.
reason: State-controlled refiner/marketer whose adjusted EPS swings with crack spreads and government fuel-pricing policy (INR 4.09 in 2022 to 62.6 in 2023, margin at 91st pctile, consensus FY1 -66%); commodity and policy driven.

name: JK Tyre & Industries Ltd.
reason: Cyclical tyre maker with 10y adjusted EPS CAGR of 4.6% (INR 24.34 in 2015 to 38.08 in 2025), 6% avg ROIC, rubber-cost-driven margins and acquisition-funded growth (Cavendish; acq/FCF 1.76) with negative 10y FCF conversion; ordinary cyclical.

name: Deepak Fertilisers & Petrochemicals Corp. Ltd.
reason: Ammonia/nitric-acid/fertiliser producer with EPS set by gas and chemical prices (INR 97.2 in 2022 to 35.65 in 2023), -0.72 10y FCF conversion and net debt/EBITDA 3.1x on heavy capex; commodity chemicals with no moat.

name: GAIL (India) Ltd.
reason: State-owned gas transmission/trading/petchem company whose EPS swings with LNG spreads and petchem prices (INR 15.53 in 2021 to 8.17 in 2022 to 10.89 in 2025) and regulated tariffs; commodity/policy earnings, 0.25 FCF conversion.

name: Petronet LNG Ltd.
reason: PSU-promoted LNG regas monopoly with 23% avg ROE but growth has stalled (adjusted EPS INR 23.57 in 2023 to 25.62 in 2025, 5y CAGR 5.4%, LTG 2.5%) while Dahej tariff pressure and a large petchem capex push FCF negative; no route to >=7% EPS growth.

name: Steel Authority of India Ltd.
reason: State-owned steelmaker with commodity-driven EPS (losses 2015-19, INR 30.17 in 2021 then 8.95 in 2025), 10y avg ROE 5.7% and consensus FY2-3 declines; fails commodity and quality tests.

name: Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Ltd.
reason: Rural vehicle-finance NBFC with a credit-cycle record (EPS INR 15.0 in 2018 to 2.93 in 2020, now at 10y high of 20.48), 10y avg ROE only 10.3% and 3.6%/yr share dilution; not best-in-class through cycles under the US lender standard.

name: LT Foods Ltd.
reason: Branded basmati leader (Daawat/Royal) with adjusted EPS INR 2.71 to 25.1 (24.9% 10y CAGR) and 15.8% avg ROE, but paddy-price and export-policy exposure, thin 8% margins, 0.43 FCF conversion, a 19% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and US tariff risk on its largest market make 10-year earnings hard to forecast.

name: YES BANK Ltd.
reason: Failed and rescued bank (EPS INR 18.06 in 2017 to -56.07 in 2019, 1.11 in 2025) with 30.8%/yr share dilution and -1.7% 10y avg ROE; fails credit record and capital tests outright.

name: Karur Vysya Bank Ltd.
reason: Mid-sized South Indian bank whose EPS fell from INR 6.57 (2015) to 2.21 (2018) through the bad-loan cycle and is now at a 10y high of 25.97 on benign credit, with 10.8% avg ROE; not through-cycle best-in-class under the US bank standard.

name: SJVN Ltd.
reason: State-owned hydro generator with declining EPS (INR 4.13 in 2020 to 1.30 in 2025, 10y CAGR -10.2%), net debt/EBITDA 8.6x and deeply negative FCF on a debt-funded renewables build-out; regulated returns with deteriorating record.

name: Five-Star Business Finance Ltd.
reason: Small-business secured lender with a strong record (EPS INR 1.92 in 2017 to 37.25 in 2025, 16.4% avg ROE) but growth stalled in 2025 (+2%) as MSME/LAP asset quality weakened, the public record dates only from 2022 and earnings depend on an untested informal-borrower credit cycle.

name: Indian Railway Finance Corp. Ltd.
reason: State-owned captive financier to Indian Railways on a cost-plus lease model: near-zero credit risk but EPS growth has slowed to ~3%/yr (INR 4.85 in 2022 to 5.36 in 2025) as the railway budget shifts funding away, with net debt/EBITDA ~16x; no >=7% route and policy-set economics.

name: Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd.
reason: Solar module/cell maker with a 4-year record whose EPS jumped from INR 0.49 (2023) to 17.17 (2025) with EBIT margin at a record 29.4% (100th pctile) on policy-protected (ALMM) pricing, while capacity floods in and FCF is negative; peak-cycle commodity manufacturer.

name: Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Ltd.
reason: State-owned renewable-energy lender with EPS INR 3.23 to 6.73 (7.6% 10y CAGR) but a -53% year in 2022, 11.7%/yr share dilution, 9.5x leverage and concentrated project-credit exposure under government policy direction; cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Manappuram Finance Ltd.
reason: Gold-loan/microfinance NBFC whose EPS fell from INR 25.97 (2023) to 10.85 (2025) on microfinance credit losses and an RBI embargo on its Asirvad subsidiary, now passing to Bain Capital control; gold-price and credit-cycle earnings with governance change.

name: Ntpc Ltd.
reason: State-owned regulated generator with a steady record (adjusted EPS INR 9.5 to 26.89, 11% 10y CAGR, no down year) but margin at its 100th pctile, net debt/EBITDA 4.5x, negative FCF on a large renewables/nuclear capex plan and returns set by the CERC regulator and government policy.

name: Axis Bank Ltd.
reason: Large private bank whose credit record failed the zero-rate test (EPS INR 34.58 in 2015 to 1.09 in 2017 and 5.87 in 2019, 10y avg ROE 9.5%) before rebounding to 78.9; not through-cycle best-in-class under the US bank standard despite 18% consensus LTG.
